metadata.note: Midland Valley Railroad (Arkansas corporation, 1903; controlled by the Muskogee Company of Philadelphia) - Fort Smith AR - Muskogee - Tulsa - Pawhuska OK - Arkansas City - Wichita KS. MV ran every passenger train on every span drawn, including over Frisco (Fort Smith - Rock Island) and MoPac (Silverdale - Arkansas City) trackage and on the leased Wichita and Midland Valley, so all features take MV's company and colour; no Rule 4 split (Texas & Pacific / Missouri Pacific control 1964/1967 came 30 years after passenger service ended). Passenger service Fort Smith - Pawhuska ended Oct 1934. Drawn: main-line blocks [1]-[6] of the research report, each to its drawable span.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (Sept 1951 data), Midland Valley tables 'For Freight Train Service only' (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)
metadata.branches_deliberately_omitted: [7] Hartford Branch (Rock Island - Hackett - Excelsior - Hartford AR, ~23.7 mi): passenger service proven by an undated Condren photo and Fowler's station list, but no year confirmed - drawable NONE. [8] Excelsior - Greenwood AR (6.25 mi): no confirmable passenger year - drawable NONE. [9] Glenpool Branch (Jenks - Glenpool - Kiefer, 8.65 mi): oil-field branch, no dated passenger evidence - drawable NONE. Also not drawn: all post-1934 freight operation (Rule 1).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] Pawhuska - Arkansas City drawn 1906-1911 and [OPEN] Arkansas City - Wichita drawn 1911-1928: both ends are the last CONFIRMED years, not known ends. Condren's timeline scopes the Oct 1934 end to 'Ft. Smith to Pawhuska' and adds '(mixed service continues to MP control)'; a trainorders.com poster recalls an undated tri-weekly Pawhuska - Wichita mixed; Wikipedia gives 1934 system-wide; the Sept 1951 Official Guide prints all MV tables freight-only. A dated 1912-1964 MV timetable, or a Kansas/Oklahoma Corporation Commission discontinuance order, or 1934 Arkansas City Traveler / Wichita Eagle coverage would settle it. (2) The three 1934 end sources (Condren, Wikipedia, Bixby HS) may not be independent; Hal Miller, 'Muskogee Roads: a four state empire', Classic Trains Spring 2008, is the best single source to check. (3) Start years: no ICC 'operation began' dates; Muskogee (1904?) and Tulsa (1904/05?) openings are bracketed, so the 1906 starts may be 1-2 years late; Fort Smith - Rock Island start bracket 1904-1908. (4) Pawhuska geometry: the ICC lists a 'six-mile motor car route between Nelagoney and Pawhuska' as joint use; whether Pawhuska sat on MV's own main line (as Fowler's sequence and this trace assume) or on a joint stub over the Santa Fe is unresolved. (5) Hartford Branch, Excelsior - Greenwood and Glenpool Branch need a dated passenger year before they can be drawn. (6) Whether any mail/express-only motor-car runs survived 1934 (would not count as passenger service anyway). (7) All headways and avg_speed_kmh are estimates; the 1933 Tulsa - Fort Smith motor-car times come from an uncited forum post.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, traced with opstrace.py; see each feature's geometry_source.

metadata.horsecar_audit: Not applicable: MV was steam from the start, with gasoline motor cars from 1913. Nothing trimmed.

properties.line: Midland Valley: Fort Smith – Rock Island (Frisco trackage)
properties.speed_source: estimated. The only running time seen is a 1933 schedule quoted in a forum post (MV #2 motor car lv Tulsa 4:00pm, ar Fort Smith 10:10pm: ~159 mi in 6h10 = ~42 km/h), with no timetable cited; the figure is applied to the whole road as an estimate. Rule 3.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) plus OpenHistoricalMap, traced with opstrace.py (operator-weighted routing; OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator='Midland Valley' or named 'Midland Valley Railroad' at 1x, untagged abandoned/razed grade at 1.25x, any other named operator at 12x). This feature was traced with the Frisco as the preferred operator, since MV ran over the St. Louis-San Francisco: 15.7 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator=Frisco, chiefly the live 'CPKC Fort Smith Branch' (way 1025890710), with the last stretch into Fort Smith on track named 'Arkansas and Missouri Railroad', also tagged old_railway_operator=Frisco. Waypoints: Fort Smith (Nominatim city, 0.66 km from the line), a pin on way 1025890710 north of Rock Island, and Rock Island / Maney Jct pinned where the MV grade (OSM way 165936947, old_railway_operator=Midland Valley) meets the ex-Frisco line (-94.4730, 35.1818), 0.4 km east of Nominatim's Rock Island.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 15.7 mi against a documented 15.84 mi of joint track (ICC valuation) and 16.3 mi (Fowler MP 305.5-321.8): within 4%. No approximated (straight-line) legs. TRACKAGE RIGHTS: this is Frisco (St. Louis-San Francisco) track, the Fort Smith - Paris TX line; the feature carries Midland Valley's company and colour because MV ran the trains (Rule 4). The Frisco Mansfield Branch, which MV crossed but never used, was deliberately avoided (a first trace that routed onto it was rejected). LATER ALIGNMENT: drawn on the present-day CPKC Fort Smith Branch, the same ex-Frisco line as it survives today; Fort Smith terminal trackage has changed since 1934 and the line ends at the city centre (0.66 km), not at the Frisco station / MV Parker Ave depot, which was not located.

segments.note: Midland Valley passenger trains over the St. Louis-San Francisco (Frisco) Fort Smith - Paris line, Fort Smith - Cedars - Rock Island (Maney Jct), OK: 15.84 mi of joint track (ICC valuation), MV's only entry into Fort Smith; MV used the Frisco passenger station (later its own Parker Ave depot). Start 1908 is the first CONFIRMED year: Ingersoll's papers show MV paying in 1908 for use of the Frisco passenger station and running 6 trains a day over this track. The Fort Smith terminal tracks were built 1904, so service probably began between 1904 and 1908; earlier years are unconfirmed, not absent. End Oct 1934: Condren's Fort Smith railroad timeline ('Midland Valley ends passenger service - Ft. Smith to Pawhuska, OK'); Wikipedia and the Bixby Historical Society also give 1934. These three may all derive from one secondary source (possibly Hal Miller, 'Muskogee Roads', Classic Trains, Spring 2008, not consulted). Headway 480 min derived from '6 trains a day' (both directions) in 1908 - an estimate, not a timetable figure. Freight-only in the Sept 1951 Official Guide.
sources: Segment-level: per research/branches/midland_valley_railroad.txt (2026-11-17), start 1908 from the Ingersoll papers via Condren's MV historical info page; end Oct 1934 from Condren's Fort Smith timeline; headway derived from the 1908 '6 trains a day' figure.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 88.2 mi against a documented ~88 mi (Fowler MP 217.4-305.5 = 88.1 mi). Approximated legs: two hand-added straight bridges between OSM abandoned-grade fragments that do not touch - 0.63 km (0.4 mi) at Stigler (between ways 390079424 and 262217703) and 1.84 km (1.1 mi) between Warner and Keefeton (between ways 14907124 and 14904317), total 1.5 mi; without them the router fell back to 7.5 mi and 7.2 mi chords. The first 1.13 km, from the Frisco crossing at Rock Island west along the MV grade (way 165936947, which runs nearly straight here), is a straight join because the router's start snapped west of the junction. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the grade as OSM maps it today, i.e. the road's last alignment before abandonment; any pre-abandonment realignment is not shown. The ICC valuation records a 5.73 mi line revision built Jul 1908 - Apr 1909, so for 1906-1908 this draws the post-revision alignment over that stretch (location not identified).

segments.note: Midland Valley main line, First District: Rock Island (Maney Jct) - Panama - Bokoshe - Keota - Stigler - Porum - Warner - Keefeton - Muskogee (~88 mi, Fowler mileposts 217.4-305.5). Built 1903-1904 (ICC valuation); Okhistory says MV 'reached Muskogee in 1904'. Start 1906 is the first CONFIRMED year (MoPac history: 292.7 mi open Silverdale KS - Hoye/Fidelity AR by May 1, 1906); no ICC 'operation began' date was found, so 1904-1905 passenger years are unconfirmed, not absent. Through trains ran Fort Smith - Muskogee - Tulsa. End Oct 1934: Condren's Fort Smith railroad timeline ('Midland Valley ends passenger service - Ft. Smith to Pawhuska, OK'); Wikipedia and the Bixby Historical Society also give 1934. These three may all derive from one secondary source (possibly Hal Miller, 'Muskogee Roads', Classic Trains, Spring 2008, not consulted). Headway 720 min is an estimate (two trains each way a day assumed by analogy with the Bixby figure on the Muskogee - Tulsa section); not from a timetable. After 1934 freight only (MV, then MoPac); Excelsior - Panama abandoned 1968. The Feb 1, 1958 head-on collision of freights 41/42 at Bokoshe is not passenger evidence.
sources: Segment-level: per research/branches/midland_valley_railroad.txt (2026-11-17), start 1906 from MoPac's 'open by May 1, 1906' (an opening statement, not an explicit passenger timetable); end Oct 1934 from Condren's timeline, Wikipedia and Bixby HS. Headway NOT SOURCED (estimate).

Approximated legs: a 0.48 km join at Muskogee to the end of the Rock Island - Muskogee feature, and a 0.39 km hand-added bridge between abandoned-grade fragments between Leonard and Bixby (ways 1416338234 and 15047220). Tulsa end: drawn to Tulsa city centre beside Union Station, which MV used from 1917 under a shared-track agreement with the Santa Fe; the pre-1917 MV station is not separately drawn. segments.note: Midland Valley main line Muskogee - Taft - Haskell - Leonard - Bixby - Jenks - Lefeber (Red Fork) - Tulsa (MV station; Tulsa Union Station from 1917 under a shared-track agreement with the Santa Fe). 57.94 mi built Apr 1904 - Jan 1905 (ICC valuation). Start 1906 is the first CONFIRMED year (MoPac: open by May 1, 1906); Okhistory says Tulsa was reached 1905, Wikipedia 1904 - construction dates, not service dates, so 1905 is unconfirmed rather than absent. The busiest MV passenger section: Bixby HS says four trains a day passed Leonard and Bixby with a postal car (undated) - headway 720 min derived from that, an estimate. Aug 1916: MV ran 'an up-to-date motor car service between Muskogee and Tulsa without stop' (Wichita Beacon, Tihen notes). Last dated sighting: MV 2-8-0 #12 on a passenger train at Tulsa, May 1934. Bixby HS: 'It stopped carrying passengers in 1934.' End Oct 1934: Condren's Fort Smith railroad timeline ('Midland Valley ends passenger service - Ft. Smith to Pawhuska, OK'); Wikipedia and the Bixby Historical Society also give 1934. These three may all derive from one secondary source (possibly Hal Miller, 'Muskogee Roads', Classic Trains, Spring 2008, not consulted). Freight ran until 1986 (flood washed out a bridge near Leonard).
sources: Segment-level: per research/branches/midland_valley_railroad.txt (2026-11-17), start 1906 from MoPac's 'open by May 1, 1906'; end 1934 from Bixby HS, Wikipedia and Condren's timeline; headway derived from Bixby HS 'four trains a day' (undated).

segments.note: Midland Valley main line through the Osage Nation: Tulsa - Turley - Sperry - Skiatook - Avant - Barnsdall - Nelagony - Pawhuska (~49 mi, Fowler 113.9-162.9), part of the ICC valuation's Tulsa - Silverdale section built Jan 1905 - Jun 1906. Start 1906 is the first CONFIRMED year (MoPac: open through to Silverdale by May 1, 1906; Okhistory has Barnsdall reached 1905). End Oct 1934: Condren's timeline names this exact span ('Ft. Smith to Pawhuska'); Wikipedia agrees. The ICC valuation also lists a 'six-mile motor car route between Nelagoney and Pawhuska' under joint-use arrangements - unresolved; Fowler places Pawhuska on the MV main line (Myers 106.2 - Pawhuska 113.9 - Nelagony 119.6), and that is what is drawn. Headway 720 min is an estimate. MoPac closed the line north of Barnsdall in 1968; Tulsa - Skiatook is now the Osage Prairie Trail.

segments.note: [OPEN] Midland Valley main line Pawhuska - Myers - Pearsonia - Foraker - Grainola - Hardy - Silverdale KS, then 9.03 mi of joint Missouri Pacific track Silverdale - Arkansas City (ICC valuation) plus MV's own 2.14 mi connection into Arkansas City (Jul 1905 - Mar 1906). Start 1906: Wichita Beacon, Mar 8, 1906, MV 'has completed its line to Arkansas City'; MoPac: open from Silverdale by May 1, 1906. END 1911 IS THE LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END: the last dated through working is the first regular Fort Smith - Wichita through passenger train, Oct 4, 1911 (Tihen notes). Service certainly ran longer. Candidate ends: 1934 (Wikipedia, system-wide), or a post-1934 mixed train (Condren's timeline: Oct 1934 end is 'Ft. Smith to Pawhuska ... mixed service continues to MP control'; an undated trainorders.com recollection of a tri-weekly Pawhuska - Wichita mixed) - neither is confirmed for this section. The Sept 1951 Official Guide prints the whole MV 'For Freight Train Service only' and daggers Hardy, Grainola and Pawhuska freight-only, so the end is before 1951. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: [OPEN] Wichita and Midland Valley Railroad (leased to MV from Mar 14, 1911, before opening; MV ran every train - not an ownership split): Arkansas City - Geuda Springs - Adamsville - Oxford - Palestine - Belle Plaine - Wichita (MV station at the west end of the Douglas Ave bridge), 50.04 mi (W&MV ICC valuation). Built 1911 (completed into Wichita Sep 13). Start Oct 4, 1911: Wichita Beacon, Oct 3, 1911 - 'the first regular passenger train will whistle in the new Midland Valley station ... the regular through passenger train running from Ft. Smith'. Aug 1913: a 98-seat gasoline motor car began a daily Arkansas City - Wichita run (Beacon/Eagle, Aug 1913). END 1928 IS THE LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END: an MV passenger train photographed at Wichita in 1928 (4-4-0s #33 and #35, Louis Marre coll.). Service probably continued to 1934 or later, but that is unconfirmed here; the Sept 1951 Official Guide daggers Palestine and Geuda Springs freight-only. Freight to Wichita ended 1966 and the line washed out in 1967 - freight dates, not passenger ends. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 min is an estimate (one through train plus the 1913 motor car each way).
